rules: Change only through scripts/feature.py. Build sessions change status and notes; planning sessions add features and edit todo or blocked ones. Never delete or reword acceptance criteria of a started feature; raise a question instead. Every feature has 2-8 criteria, owned paths (globs) and the evidence it must attach.

features.title: Rust workspace scaffold
acceptance: The Cargo workspace SHALL contain every crate in 01-architecture.md#repository-layout plus tests/fake-provider (crate lecter-fake-provider), each named lecter-<folder> and each with one real smoke test.
Root Cargo.toml SHALL set [workspace.package] version = "0.0.1" and edition 2024, and rust-toolchain.toml SHALL pin the current stable toolchain (recorded in one D-entry with the Node and pnpm pins).
deny.toml SHALL allow exactly the licences in 01-architecture.md#dependency-policy and deny unknown registries and git sources; `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` SHALL pass.
crates/cli SHALL build a `lecter` binary that prints its version and nothing else (v1 builds the rest).
.gitattributes SHALL force LF for text files and mark binary fixtures as binary.
verify: cargo deny check licenses bans sources

features.title: UI scaffold with mocked core
acceptance: ui/ SHALL be Vite + SolidJS + TypeScript (strict, no implicit any) with Biome, Vitest and Playwright, and package.json `packageManager` and `engines` SHALL pin the Node LTS and pnpm versions.
ui/package.json SHALL provide the scripts `build`, `test:e2e`, `test:e2e:smoke`, `lint:dup` (jscpd) and `lint:unused` (knip) that scripts/verify.sh calls.
ui/e2e/mock-core/ SHALL provide a mocked core that Playwright tests use instead of Tauri IPC.
One Playwright test tagged @smoke SHALL load the app shell against the mocked core in Chromium.
ui/playwright.config.ts SHALL set retries: 0 and the smoke project to Chromium only.
features.try: Run pnpm -C ui run dev and open the printed URL: the shell renders against the mocked core

features.title: Tauri shell and dev script
acceptance: app/ SHALL be a Tauri 2 shell (crate lecter-app) whose tauri.conf.json sets identifier io.github.jaykuroor.lecter, version 0.0.1 and the CSP of SEC-30 exactly.
The main window's capability file SHALL list only the commands the shell uses (SEC-31), and no capability SHALL name a remote URL.
Release builds SHALL have devtools disabled (SEC-34); a test SHALL assert the release config.
WHEN `scripts/dev.sh` runs THEN the app SHALL open one window showing the UI shell with hot reload.
The identifier SHALL appear only in app/tauri.conf.json; Rust SHALL read it at build time into lecter_core::identity::APP_ID.
features.try: Run scripts/dev.sh: one Lecter window opens

features.title: CI workflows and verify stages
acceptance: .github/workflows/ci.yml SHALL implement the `lint`, `test` (ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, windows-2025) and `e2e` jobs of 16-ci-cd.md with those exact names, each calling `scripts/verify.sh --stage <name>`.
Every workflow SHALL start with `permissions: contents: read` and pin third-party actions by commit SHA with the version in a comment.
ci.yml SHALL use the concurrency group from 16-ci-cd.md, cache Rust and pnpm, and install cargo-nextest, cargo-deny and a checksum-verified gitleaks binary.
.github/dependabot.yml SHALL group weekly updates for github-actions, cargo and npm (ui/) with at most 3 open PRs each.
WHEN `scripts/init.sh` runs on a clean checkout THEN it SHALL install dependencies, build, and print `INIT OK`; `scripts/init.sh --check` SHALL list missing tools with Fedora install commands.
verify: act or a pushed run (UNVERIFIED-ON macos, windows until CI runs)

features.title: Code-health gates
acceptance: Workspace lints SHALL deny clippy::unwrap_used and clippy::expect_used outside tests (clippy.toml allow-unwrap-in-tests and allow-expect-in-tests).

clippy.toml disallowed-methods SHALL ban std::thread::sleep, std::fs::* and std::net::* blocking calls in async crates, and Tauri's identifier-based path helpers (app_config_dir, app_data_dir, app_cache_dir, app_local_data_dir); a fixture SHALL show each is reported.
scripts/check_arch.py SHALL pass on the real workspace, and a test fixture with a core → ai dependency SHALL make it fail.
jscpd (lint:dup) SHALL fail on a copied block of 30+ lines in ui/src or crates, and knip (lint:unused) SHALL fail on an unused export.
scripts/check_size.py SHALL pass on the scaffold (file-length limit 500 lines for .rs, .ts and .tsx outside generated files).

features.title: Spike: CodeMirror lecture surface performance
acceptance: A throwaway prototype in spikes/editor SHALL render a 200-slide fixture with KaTeX blocks, gloss widgets and Vim mode in one CodeMirror buffer.
A script SHALL measure p99 keystroke-to-paint and heap size in Chromium and WebKit (Playwright) and record the numbers and a go/no-go in a D-entry.

features.title: Spike: parse-worker OS sandboxes
acceptance: spikes/os-sandbox SHALL be a workspace test crate whose child process, once sandboxed, cannot open a network socket, read a file other than its input, or exceed 1 GB, each asserted by a test.
The tests SHALL implement Linux seccomp + Landlock, a macOS sandbox profile, and a Windows AppContainer or restricted token plus job object, selected by cfg(target_os).
Linux results SHALL be measured locally; macOS and Windows results SHALL come from the `test` CI job (report UNVERIFIED-ON until CI runs), and the go/no-go per OS SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.
features.notes: BLOCKED: IMPOSSIBLE: crit 1 on Windows (LPAC reads files granted to ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES, e.g. win.ini) - SEC-01 Windows wording change, Q-008. Linux/macOS GO. Branch feat/F-005-os-sandbox. | Builder's final commit a8e5aa5 on feat/F-005-os-sandbox (pushed up to c8900b7; push again before merging).

features.title: Spike: PDFium bundling per OS
acceptance: A script SHALL download the pinned PDFium build for linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-universal, windows-x64 and windows-arm64 and verify each SHA-256 before use (SEC-51).
A workspace test SHALL load PDFium dynamically through pdfium-render and extract page-1 text from a synthetic fixture PDF on all three CI OSes.
The D-entry SHALL record the source, version, licence, per-OS size and how the bundle step will place the library.
features.ask_jay_first: PDFium is a native binary. Approve the source (for example bblanchon/pdfium-binaries, BSD/Apache) and pinning by SHA-256 per OS?

features.title: Spike: vision parsing quality and cost
acceptance: Through scripts/live.sh, the spike SHALL compare provider fast vision with PaddleOCR-VL (CPU) on private manifest items of every kind_guess plus public synthetic files, reporting CER, LaTeX exact match, seconds per page, tokens and cost per page, by manifest id only.
The script SHALL respect LECTER_LIVE_RPM and LECTER_LIVE_RPD, back off on 429 with retry-after and jitter, and save partial results at the daily cap.
The results and the recommended parsing.vision default SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.

features.title: Spike: retrieval eval
acceptance: On a synthetic fixture course (1 textbook, 10 lectures, 40 questions with reference passages) the spike SHALL measure recall@5 and p95 latency for BM25, BM25+local-small, BM25+local-quality and BM25+provider embeddings (provider calls through scripts/live.sh, rate-limited).
The chosen index.embeddings default SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.

features.title: Spike: TTFT per provider with caching
acceptance: Through scripts/live.sh, the spike SHALL measure TTFT and cached-token ratio for a 20k-token prefix on each provider with a key (Gemini at least), cold vs warm connection, cached vs uncached, within the free-tier rate limits.
The results SHALL be recorded in a D-entry, naming providers that were skipped for lack of a key.

features.title: Harness binary and test home
acceptance: crates/harness SHALL build a `lecter-harness` binary that is never part of an app bundle.
`lecter-harness <command> --json` SHALL print one JSON result per call, and errors as `{"error":{"code":…}}` with the codes of 18-contracts.md#error-codes and a non-zero exit.
WHEN LECTER_TEST_HOME is set THEN every config, data and cache path SHALL resolve under it (unit-tested), so tests never touch real folders.
`lecter-harness version` SHALL print the workspace version; each later skeleton feature adds its own subcommand.

features.title: Drive the real app: embedded WebDriver
acceptance: tauri-plugin-wdio-webdriver SHALL be a dependency only under cfg(debug_assertions) (or the test-hooks feature) and registered only there.
tests/e2e/ SHALL hold a WebdriverIO setup (@wdio/tauri-service, driverProvider embedded) and one flow that opens the app and asserts the shell is visible.

`scripts/e2e-app.sh [flow] [--evidence F-0NN]` SHALL build the debug app, run the flows (under xvfb-run on Linux, with WEBKIT_DISABLE_SANDBOX_THIS_IS_DANGEROUS=1 set only for these debug runs so WebKitGTK works inside the Claude Code sandbox) and, with --evidence, save screenshots and app.log to .evidence/F-0NN/.
LECTER_TEST_PICK and LECTER_TEST_TRUST SHALL answer native dialogs in debug builds, proven by a flow that opens a folder without a dialog appearing.
ci.yml SHALL gain the `e2e-app` job (ubuntu-24.04 under xvfb-run, macos-15, windows-2025) and the `release-check` job running scripts/check_release_binary.sh.
A release-profile build SHALL pass scripts/check_release_binary.sh, and a debug build SHALL fail it (both asserted).

features.title: IPC contract and generated bindings
acceptance: Commands and events SHALL be declared once in app/src/ipc/ and exported with tauri-specta (or the maintained alternative chosen in a D-entry) to ui/src/core/bindings.ts.
`cargo run -p lecter-app --bin export-bindings -- --check` SHALL exit non-zero when the committed bindings are stale, and scripts/verify.sh SHALL run it (bindings-stale).
ui/e2e/mock-core SHALL implement the generated Commands type, so a mock that drifts from the contract fails `tsc`.

IpcError SHALL carry the codes of 18-contracts.md#error-codes, and a shared validator SHALL reject strings, lists and payloads over the limits in 18-contracts.md#validation with E_INVALID_ARGUMENT (tested per limit).
The overhead of Tauri's isolation pattern per call SHALL be measured and the decision recorded in a D-entry (SEC-36).

features.title: Skeleton: open a course folder
acceptance: `course_open` SHALL accept only a folder chosen in a dialog this session (or LECTER_TEST_PICK) and return its lectures/ and slides/ listing.
Paths SHALL be canonicalised and symlinks escaping the course root rejected with E_NOT_TRUSTED (tested with a symlink fixture).
The opened course SHALL appear in the UI, proven by a WebDriver flow with a screenshot.
`lecter-harness course open <dir>` SHALL print the same listing as JSON.
features.try: Open a course folder (any folder with a slides/ subfolder)

features.title: Skeleton: parse one text PDF in the worker
acceptance: lecter-parse SHALL run as a child process speaking the worker protocol of 18-contracts.md#worker-protocol, with a Hello version check.
A synthetic text-layer fixture PDF SHALL become blocks with page numbers and reading order via PDFium (tested).
WHEN the worker crashes or exceeds 60 s THEN the core SHALL mark the file E_PARSE_FAILED and stay responsive (tested with a crashing fixture).
`lecter-harness parse <pdf>` SHALL print the blocks as JSON.

features.title: Skeleton: lecture buffer with Vim keys
acceptance: Opening a lecture SHALL render its parsed slide blocks in one CodeMirror buffer styled from docs/design/components.md (slide heading, block).
j, k, gg and G SHALL move between blocks in normal mode, and i and Esc SHALL switch insert and normal mode (WebDriver flow).
The 200-slide fixture lecture SHALL keep keystroke-to-paint p99 under 8 ms in the mocked-core Playwright check.
A screenshot of the buffer SHALL be attached and compared with docs/design/reference/buffer-*.png by the reviewer.
features.try: Open a lecture; move with j/k, type with i, leave with Esc

features.title: Skeleton: save, journal, survive restart
acceptance: Every edit SHALL be appended to the journal in the record format of 18-contracts.md#journal-records within 250 ms.
The .md SHALL be written via temp file, fsync and atomic rename, debounced to 1 s.
WHEN the app is killed with SIGKILL during typing THEN after restart the lecture SHALL contain all but at most 250 ms of the typed text (tests/crash test).
A WebDriver flow SHALL type, quit, relaunch and see the text.
features.try: Type a note, quit Lecter, reopen: the note is still there

features.title: Skeleton: BM25 search
acceptance: Blocks of opened lectures SHALL be indexed into Tantivy with lecture, slide and block id fields.
`search_find` SHALL return ranked hits with block ids, and `:find <words>` SHALL list them in the UI (WebDriver flow).
`lecter-harness search <course> <query>` SHALL print the hits as JSON.
features.try: Type :find and a word from the lecture

features.title: Skeleton: one gloss from the fake provider
acceptance: A minimal Provider trait and the fake provider SHALL stream an answer over a typed channel (GlossStream).
Pressing a on a block, typing a question and Enter SHALL stream a gloss under that block, rendered at most once per animation frame.
The gloss SHALL be saved in the lecture as a fenced div per 03-lecture-files.md#body.
Esc SHALL cancel the stream within 50 ms (fake provider with a slow stream).
`lecter-harness prompt <lecture> <block> <question>` SHALL print the assembled request as JSON.
features.try: Press a on a line, ask something: a sample answer streams in under it

features.title: Skeleton: one described figure
acceptance: A fake-provider answer containing an fnplot spec SHALL render as a plot inside the gloss, computed locally.
The figure SHALL make no network request (asserted in the WebDriver flow).
The plot SHALL re-render only when scrolled into view.
features.try: Ask for a plot in the tutorial-style sample: a plot appears in the answer

features.title: Perf harness and budget gate
acceptance: tests/perf/budgets.json SHALL list every budget in 14-quality.md#performance-budgets with its target, kind and starting milestone.

`tests/perf/budgets.sh` SHALL measure keystroke_p99_ms, cold_open_ms, idle_rss_mb, rss_300_slides_mb, idle_cpu_pct, ttft_overhead_ms and ui_main_chunk_kb_gz on the real app and exit non-zero on a breach (×1.5 for timing with --ci).
Budgets whose feature doesn't exist yet SHALL print PENDING and fail once their starting milestone is done.
ci.yml SHALL gain the required `perf` job, and a deliberately slowed fixture SHALL make it fail (asserted in a test of budgets.sh).
The first measurements SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.

features.title: Skeleton end to end on three OSes
acceptance: One WebdriverIO flow SHALL open a course, parse a text PDF into a lecture, edit it, restart, search it, ask for a gloss and show a figure, with a screenshot per step.
The flow SHALL pass in the `e2e-app` job on Linux, macOS and Windows (CI run linked in the report).
The same path SHALL pass through lecter-harness commands with no GUI.
features.try: Walk the whole path: open course, open lecture, edit, restart, search, ask, see a plot

features.title: Spike: Vim and IME in three webviews
acceptance: A WebDriver flow SHALL drive Vim normal and insert mode and a synthetic IME composition (compositionstart, update, end) in WebKitGTK, WKWebView and WebView2 via the e2e-app job, asserting the composed text lands once and normal-mode keys don't fire during composition.
Failures per webview and the workaround chosen SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.

features.title: Spike: figure iframe sandbox per webview
acceptance: A sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts only) with the CSP of 08-figures.md#sandbox-pages SHALL be proven, in all three webviews via the e2e-app job, unable to fetch the network, read parent DOM, use storage or call IPC.
A busy loop in the frame SHALL be detected within 2 s by the watchdog approach chosen, and the result per webview SHALL be recorded in a D-entry.

features.title: Settings core: schema, JSONC, precedence
acceptance: Settings types SHALL be defined in Rust and SHALL generate settings.schema.json (a test fails if the committed schema is stale).
The resolved value of a key SHALL follow prompt > role > course > global > default and report its source (property test).
WHEN a config file contains unknown keys THEN they SHALL be preserved on write and reported once.
WHEN a config file changes on disk THEN the new values SHALL apply within 1 s without restart.
features.notes: Add performance presets (D-081): Performance/Balanced(default)/Quality; perf toggles default Balanced. Criteria pending Q-006.

features.title: Global folders per OS
acceptance: The global config folder SHALL be ~/.config/lecter on Linux and macOS ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lecter if set) and %APPDATA%\lecter on Windows; data and cache SHALL use the folders in the identity table.
All locations SHALL derive from identity::APP_DIR_NAME and identity::KEYCHAIN_SERVICE ("lecter"); a test SHALL show they are unchanged when APP_ID changes.
WHEN no global config exists THEN first-run state SHALL be detected and onboarding flagged.

features.title: Identity migration hook
acceptance: WHEN identity::LEGACY_APP_IDS lists an old identifier with data in its locations THEN identity::migrate() SHALL move it to the stable locations (tested with a temp home).
migrate() SHALL run at most once, recorded in state.db meta.
Keychain items under a legacy service SHALL be re-saved under "lecter" (tested against a mock keychain).

features.title: Trust screen and read-only courses
acceptance: WHEN a folder is opened for the first time THEN a trust screen SHALL show counts of slides, sources and lectures, the provider that receives excerpts, and web search state.
WHEN the user picks Open read-only THEN AI, indexing and scripted figures SHALL be disabled for that course.
Trust SHALL be stored per absolute path in trusted.jsonc; WHEN the path changes THEN trust SHALL be asked again.
Every file API used by the AI SHALL reject paths outside the course root after canonicalisation (property test with .., symlinks, UNC and Windows separators).
features.try: Open a new folder: the trust screen shows what Lecter will read

features.title: Course details form
acceptance: After trusting, a form SHALL collect name, code, term, professor, icon, colour and folder mapping, pre-filled from folder names.
Saving SHALL write .lecter/course.jsonc with "version": 1.
features.try: Fill in the course details after trusting a folder

features.title: Course rail
acceptance: The rail SHALL show one icon per course, styled per docs/design/components.md#rail.
Dragging an icon SHALL reorder courses and persist the order.
Ctrl/Cmd-1..9 SHALL switch to the nth course.
features.try: Add two courses; reorder them by dragging; switch with Ctrl-1/Ctrl-2

features.title: Sidebar
acceptance: The sidebar SHALL list Dashboard, Lectures (with date and open-item badges), Lists and Sources.
␣e SHALL toggle the sidebar, and the sidebar SHALL be fully navigable with j/k, Enter and the arrow keys.
features.try: Toggle the sidebar with Space e and open a lecture from it

features.title: Key engine
acceptance: The engine SHALL support modes, multi-key sequences and counts, with bindings that depend on the focused element type.
␣ SHALL open which-key with all groups after 300 ms.
Bindings SHALL load from defaults then keymaps.jsonc; WHEN two bindings clash in one context THEN a warning SHALL list both.
Key handling SHALL never await the core; the keystroke_p99_ms budget SHALL hold on the 200-slide fixture.
verify: pnpm -C ui exec vitest run src/keys
features.try: Press Space and wait: which-key lists every group

features.title: Hint bar
acceptance: The hint bar SHALL list the keys valid for the focused element and mode, updating on every cursor move.
Hint detail SHALL follow ui.hintBar: full also shows mouse actions, compact shows keys only, off hides it.
features.try: Move between a slide line and a gloss: the hint bar changes

features.title: Keystroke overlay and read mode
acceptance: The overlay SHALL show typed keys, including pending sequences, and fade after 1.5 s; ui.keystrokes SHALL toggle it.
Read mode (␣ur, :read) SHALL hide rail, sidebar, hint bar and overlay, and restore them on exit.
features.try: Type keys and watch the overlay; try Space u r for read mode

features.title: Command line
acceptance: : SHALL open a command line with completion for commands and setting keys.
`:set key=value` SHALL validate against the schema and reject invalid values with the reason.
`:set key?` SHALL show the value and its source.
features.try: Type :set ui.keystrokes? and :set ui.keystrokes=false

features.title: Command palette and quick switcher
acceptance: Ctrl/Cmd-Shift-P SHALL list every command with its key.
Ctrl/Cmd-K SHALL fuzzy-jump to courses, lectures, lists and sources.
features.try: Press Ctrl-K and jump to a lecture by typing part of its name

features.title: Theme tokens and the bundled Lecter theme
acceptance: Every token in docs/design/tokens.json SHALL exist as a CSS custom property, light and dark, and the bundled "Lecter" theme SHALL use exactly those values.
A lint check SHALL fail on hard-coded colours in ui/src components.
The app SHALL follow the OS dark/light preference when no GTK theme applies.
verify: pnpm -C ui exec vitest run src/theme
features.try: Switch the system between light and dark: Lecter follows

features.title: Follow the GTK theme on Linux
acceptance: On Linux the app SHALL read theme name, colour scheme and accent through the settings portal, with gsettings as fallback, and update live.
@define-color values from the theme's gtk-4.0/gtk.css (else gtk-3.0) SHALL map to Lecter tokens; missing names SHALL fall back to the Lecter theme (tested with fixture themes).
Settings SHALL list installed GTK themes from the standard folders and apply a chosen one.
features.try: Change your GTK theme or accent: Lecter follows within a second

features.title: Bundled themes on macOS and Windows
acceptance: On macOS and Windows the app SHALL follow the OS accent colour.
The bundled themes (Adwaita, Yaru, Breeze, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord; light and dark) SHALL be selectable, and a GTK theme folder in ~/.themes SHALL also be offered.

features.title: Settings window (schema-driven)
acceptance: The window SHALL render controls from the schema on the pages Appearance, Keys, AI, Providers, Courses, Notes and files, Privacy, Advanced, with search.
A change SHALL write the correct file (global or course) and apply immediately.
Every control SHALL be reachable by keyboard (Tab, arrows, j/k, / filter).
features.try: Open Settings with Ctrl-, and change the hint bar detail
features.notes: Settings > Performance page with the D-081 preset and a lag note on Quality. Criteria pending Q-006.

features.title: Status line
acceptance: The status line SHALL show mode, course/lecture, slide, active model, lecture cost and a job spinner, styled per docs/design/components.md#status-line.
The mode segment SHALL change colour per mode (NORMAL, INSERT, VISUAL, COMMAND).

features.title: Block model and lossless round trip
acceptance: Reading then writing any lecture file in tests/fixtures/lectures SHALL produce byte-identical output.
Every slide block, gloss and note SHALL have a stable id, and edits elsewhere SHALL never change an id.
Property tests SHALL show anchors survive random insert and delete sequences.
Unknown content in files Lecter didn't write SHALL be preserved.

features.title: Journal replay rules
acceptance: Replay SHALL apply only records after the last checkpoint whose base matches the file on disk.
WHEN the base doesn't match THEN the records SHALL be kept aside and the external-edit flow started.
A truncated last line SHALL be ignored (fuzzed).
The crash_loss_ms budget SHALL hold in tests/crash on Linux.

features.title: Parse worker sandbox: Linux
acceptance: On Linux the worker SHALL apply seccomp and Landlock before reading input: no network, read access to its one input file only.
The worker SHALL run with a 1 GB memory limit and a 60 s time limit per file.
Tests SHALL prove a socket(), an open() of another file and a 2 GB allocation each fail inside the worker.

features.title: Parse worker sandbox: macOS
acceptance: On macOS the worker SHALL run under a sandbox profile denying network and file reads other than its input.
The same three escape tests as Linux SHALL pass in the macos-15 CI job (UNVERIFIED-ON macos until CI runs).
verify: cargo nextest run -p lecter-parse sandbox (CI macos-15)

features.title: Parse worker sandbox: Windows
acceptance: On Windows the worker SHALL run in an AppContainer (or a restricted token) inside a job object with the memory and time limits.
The same three escape tests SHALL pass in the windows-2025 CI job (UNVERIFIED-ON windows until CI runs).
verify: cargo nextest run -p lecter-parse sandbox (CI windows-2025)

features.title: Parse input limits and fuzz targets
acceptance: Zip inputs over 200 MB uncompressed, ratio over 100, over 10,000 entries or with traversal names SHALL be rejected (SEC-02).
XML SHALL not process DTDs or external entities and SHALL stop past depth 256 (SEC-03).
Files over the limits.* size, page, pixel or object-depth limits SHALL fail with E_PARSE_FAILED and a reason (SEC-04), one test per limit.
crates/parse/fuzz SHALL have a target per reader with 5–20 small seed files.

features.title: Worker lifecycle and shutdown
acceptance: Child workers SHALL die with the app: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG on Linux, a parent-watch pipe on macOS, a kill-on-close job object on Windows (ROB-40), tested by killing the parent.
Shutdown SHALL flush the journal, write pending saves, cancel jobs and kill workers within 2 s (ROB-41).

features.title: PDF text layer parsing
acceptance: PDF pages SHALL become blocks with reading order, headings, lists and columns from the text layer.
Math glyph regions SHALL be marked for vision instead of emitted as text.
The parse_100_pages_ms budget SHALL hold.
The public text-pdf corpus SHALL meet tests/corpus/thresholds.json, and private manifest items SHALL be reported by id only.

features.title: PPTX parsing
acceptance: PPTX slides SHALL yield text, tables and speaker notes as blocks.
OMML math SHALL be converted to LaTeX (golden tests).
Build order SHALL be read from p:timing and p:bldLst and exposed as build steps.

features.title: Image files as pages
acceptance: PNG, JPEG, HEIC, WebP and multi-page TIFF SHALL become pages whose regions go to ladder step 3.
Images over the pixel limit SHALL fail before decoding (SEC-04).

features.title: PDF build-step merging
acceptance: Consecutive pages with identical title, superset text and additive-only pixel diff SHALL merge into one slide with a stepper, keeping all page numbers.
]b and [b SHALL step through builds.
features.try: Open a lecture whose PDF has animation steps: they show as one slide with a stepper

features.title: New lecture and naming
acceptance: ␣fn SHALL propose number = max+1, today's date, unlinked slides newest first, and a title from the first slide.
The file name SHALL follow lectures.namePattern.
Renaming via sidebar, :rename or F2 SHALL keep all gloss anchors.
A lecture with no slides SHALL be allowed.
features.try: Create a new lecture with Space f n

features.title: Lecture buffer rendering
acceptance: Slide blocks SHALL render KaTeX math (MathML output, trust false) and figures via lecter://.
Blocks SHALL show confidence borders by tier, with a text badge on low confidence, per docs/design/components.md#block.
Only visible blocks SHALL be rendered; the keystroke_p99_ms and rss_300_slides_mb budgets SHALL hold.

features.title: lecter:// image protocol
acceptance: Page renders and crops SHALL be served via lecter://cache/<blake3>.<ext> from the content-hash cache, never through JSON IPC.
Any other lecter:// path (traversal, other folders) SHALL return 404 (SEC-33), tested.
Only images in view SHALL be requested.

features.title: Own notes and editing
acceptance: o and O SHALL open a note below and above the current block.
Double-click on editable text SHALL enter insert mode at that point; Esc SHALL return to normal mode.
Mouse selection SHALL show the toolbar Ask, Explain, Flag, Copy.
features.try: Press o under a slide line and write a note; double-click it to edit

features.title: Plain-math input suggestion
acceptance: Typing plain math (var(x+y), sum(i=1..n), xbar) SHALL show a live LaTeX suggestion accepted with Tab.
The suggestion SHALL be computed locally with no model call (asserted: no provider request).
verify: pnpm -C ui exec vitest run src/features/mathinput
features.try: Type sum(i=1..n) in a note and press Tab

features.title: Flags
acceptance: mm SHALL toggle a flag on the block and ms on the slide.
Flags SHALL be stored as .flag in the lecture file and survive a restart.
features.try: Flag a line with mm

features.title: Jump between flags, doubts and glosses
acceptance: ]f and [f SHALL jump between flags.
]d [d and ]g [g SHALL jump between doubts and glosses.

features.title: Compare and fix parse
acceptance: gx SHALL show the original crop beside the rendered parse, per docs/design/components.md#compare-parse.
i on a slide line SHALL edit it, and the fix SHALL be stored as the parse correction.
WHEN the fix matches the rendered output THEN the confidence border SHALL be removed.
features.try: Press gx on a slide line to compare it with the original

features.title: File watching and parse cache
acceptance: New or changed files in slides/ and sources/ SHALL be parsed in the background, visible slide first.
Results SHALL be cached by BLAKE3 hash, and an unchanged file SHALL never be parsed twice.
Events SHALL be debounced and coalesced (ROB-01), and the app's own writes ignored (ROB-02).
Watching SHALL be capped and SHALL skip node_modules, .git, target, .venv and .lecter/cache (ROB-03).

features.title: External edits and the course lock
acceptance: A change on disk to an open lecture SHALL be detected by hash (ROB-10).
Edits touching different block ids SHALL merge automatically and notify the user (ROB-11).
Overlapping edits SHALL show both versions and ask, never overwrite silently (ROB-11).
A second instance opening the same course SHALL get E_LOCKED and a take-over prompt; a stale lock SHALL be taken over after asking (ROB-12).
features.try: Edit an open lecture in another editor: Lecter merges or asks

features.title: Data versioning and migrations
acceptance: state.db SHALL be created with the schema of 18-contracts.md#statedb-schema and PRAGMA user_version = 1.
Migrations SHALL be forward-only with a test per step, and a newer file SHALL open read-only with a message (ROB-21).
A backup SHALL be written before any migration (ROB-22).
PRAGMA integrity_check SHALL run on open; a corrupted fixture db SHALL be rebuilt from files with the keep tables exported first (ROB-23).

features.title: File-system edge cases
acceptance: Disk full, read-only folder and permission denied SHALL give E_IO naming the file, keep the edit in the journal and retry (ROB-30), tested with fault injection.
Windows long paths and reserved names SHALL work or be avoided (ROB-31), tested with path fixtures on all OSes.
File names SHALL compare after NFC normalisation, and case-only collisions SHALL be avoided (ROB-32, ROB-33).
Cloud placeholder files SHALL never be read during scans (ROB-34), tested with a mock placeholder attribute.

features.title: Logs: rotation and redaction
acceptance: Logs SHALL rotate daily and at 10 MB, keeping 5 files (ROB-50).
With log.content = false, no prompt, answer, note or key text SHALL appear in logs (a test greps the logs after a scripted session).
Crash reports SHALL be written locally only (ROB-51).

features.title: Provider trait, OpenAI-compatible adapter, fake provider scenarios
acceptance: The Provider trait SHALL stream text, tool calls, usage and errors, and honour a cancel token.
The OpenAI-compatible adapter SHALL work against Ollama, LM Studio and OpenRouter request formats (recorded fixtures).
tests/fake-provider SHALL simulate latency, 429 with retry-after, 5xx, dropped streams, malformed SSE and unknown event types, each as a named scenario.

features.title: Anthropic adapter
acceptance: Streaming, tool use, cache_control breakpoints and native web search SHALL work against recorded fixtures.
Usage SHALL report input, cache read, cache write and output tokens.
The adapter SHALL send a pinned anthropic-version header (ROB-60).

features.title: OpenAI Responses adapter
acceptance: Streaming, tool use and structured output SHALL work against recorded fixtures.
Native web search SHALL return citations.

features.title: Gemini adapter and free-tier preset
acceptance: Streaming, tool use, Google Search grounding and implicit caching SHALL work against recorded fixtures.
A 429 naming the free tier SHALL switch the provider to the Gemini free-tier rate-limit preset and tell the user once (SEC-10).

features.title: Keychain and :connect
acceptance: :connect and Settings → Providers SHALL add a provider by key or base URL and test it immediately.
Secrets SHALL be stored only in the OS keychain under service "lecter" and never appear in files or logs (a test greps logs, config and state.db).
The Secret type SHALL redact itself in Debug and Display and zeroise on drop, and only a mask SHALL cross IPC (SEC-41).
WHEN no Secret Service is available on Linux THEN :connect SHALL show fix steps and SHALL NOT store the key anywhere (SEC-42).
features.try: Connect Gemini with :connect (your own key) and see it tested

features.title: ChatGPT sign-in
acceptance: Before implementing, the provider's current terms SHALL be re-checked and noted in a D-entry.
ChatGPT Plus/Pro browser sign-in SHALL be offered behind a build-time flag, storing tokens in the keychain.
Anthropic SHALL offer API key only, with an explanation.
features.try: Sign in with ChatGPT under Settings → Providers

features.title: Device-code sign-in: GitHub Copilot and xAI
acceptance: GitHub Copilot and xAI SuperGrok device-code sign-in SHALL each be offered behind a build-time flag.
The device-code flow SHALL time out and cancel cleanly (tested against a fake authorisation server).

features.title: Model catalog and model selection
acceptance: The models.dev catalog SHALL be cached and refreshed weekly, and manual models SHALL be allowed.
default-fast and default-strong SHALL be chosen at connect time and be changeable; per-role and per-prompt overrides SHALL apply.
Rolling TTFT and tokens/s per model SHALL be stored in state.db.

features.title: Agent loop
acceptance: The loop SHALL run independent tools in parallel and enforce max_steps and the time budget.
Esc SHALL stop the loop and its stream within 50 ms.
Each request SHALL log tokens, latency, cost and role to state.db usage.
The ttft_overhead_ms budget SHALL hold against the fake provider.

features.title: Outbound rate limiting and retries
acceptance: Each provider SHALL have a token bucket for requests and tokens per minute, configurable per provider, with catalog defaults (SEC-10).
Queued requests SHALL wait rather than fail and SHALL report E_RATE_LIMITED with the wait time to the UI.
retry-after SHALL be honoured, with exponential backoff and full jitter, at most 3 retries, and only before the first shown token (SEC-11), tested against fake-provider scenarios.

features.title: Spend caps and usage
acceptance: Caps per gloss (output tokens, tool calls, steps), per lecture, per day and per month SHALL be enforced (SEC-12).
Background jobs SHALL have their own daily cap and SHALL pause at it.
A hedged request SHALL count against the budget, and hedging SHALL be skipped when it would exceed it.
WHEN a foreground request would exceed a cap THEN the UI SHALL ask first (E_BUDGET card), and the status line SHALL show the lecture's running cost.
features.try: Set a tiny lecture budget with :set and ask twice: Lecter asks before spending more

features.title: Coalescing, debounce, concurrency cap, timeouts
acceptance: Identical in-flight requests SHALL be coalesced into one (SEC-13), tested with a held key.
User-triggered AI actions SHALL be debounced by 150 ms.
A global concurrency cap (default 4) SHALL apply across providers.
Every network call SHALL have connect, first-byte, idle-stream and total timeouts (SEC-14), each tested with a stalled fake server.

features.title: Roles and the AI harness settings page
acceptance: Built-in role files SHALL load, overridable by global then course files.
Settings → AI SHALL edit per-role model, tools, web search, max steps, output cap, top-k, detail and prompt, writing an override file.

features.title: Prompt assembly and caching
acceptance: Tier 0 SHALL be assembled in the fixed order with cache breakpoints, and untrusted text SHALL be wrapped in <untrusted_source> (SEC-20).
Two identical requests SHALL produce byte-identical prefixes (test).
A 1-token warm-up request SHALL be sent when a lecture opens, if caching is enabled.
insta snapshots SHALL pin the exact prompt layout per provider.

features.title: Gloss lifecycle in the UI
acceptance: Answers SHALL stream into a gloss rendered at most once per animation frame, styled per docs/design/components.md#gloss in its streaming, done and focused states.
Glosses SHALL be saved as fenced divs with the prompt as the first line.
Each gloss kind SHALL use its colour token (k-*) from docs/design/tokens.json.

features.title: Gloss actions: regenerate, rate, variants
acceptance: r SHALL regenerate and R SHALL regenerate with feedback.
zg and zw SHALL rate the gloss, stored in state.db ratings.
g- and g+ SHALL switch between variants stored in state.db variants.
Ctrl-a and Ctrl-x SHALL ask for more or less detail.
features.try: On a gloss: r to regenerate, g- / g+ to switch versions, zg to rate

features.title: Gloss editing keys
acceptance: za SHALL fold and unfold a gloss.
dd SHALL delete a gloss with undo, and yy SHALL copy it.
i SHALL edit a gloss and mark it by=you+ai.

features.title: Keycap buttons
acceptance: Selecting a gloss SHALL show 3D keycap buttons for every available key, styled per docs/design/components.md#keycap.
Clicking a keycap SHALL run its command, and typing the key SHALL animate the matching button.
Reduced motion SHALL make the press instant.
features.try: Select a gloss: keycap buttons appear; click one and type one

features.title: Prompt row
acceptance: Tab SHALL toggle into this gloss / new gloss, with the documented defaults.
Enter SHALL send, Shift-Enter SHALL add a line, and Esc SHALL cancel and stop the stream.
↑ and ↓ SHALL recall previous prompts.

features.title: Prompt row mentions and toggles
acceptance: @ SHALL offer slides, lectures, sources, models, @web and @noweb.
The globe toggle SHALL set web search for that prompt only, and the model picker SHALL override the model for that prompt only.

features.title: Steps with numeric checks
acceptance: s SHALL return structured steps rendered as they arrive.
The cas crate SHALL check consecutive steps numerically and mark ✓ or –, within 5 ms per pair.
A failing step SHALL be regenerated once.
features.try: Press s on a line: steps appear with check marks

features.title: Parked doubts
acceptance: D SHALL park a doubt that runs in the background and shows its status.
A parked doubt SHALL survive an app restart and finish.
features.try: Press D on a line, keep working: the answer arrives later

features.title: Define, example and write roles
acceptance: K SHALL define the terms in the line.
x SHALL give a worked example.
> SHALL write the requested text into a gloss.

features.title: Tidy and selection ask
acceptance: gq SHALL tidy a note, keeping the original folded.
v…a SHALL ask about the selected text only.
␣ag SHALL ask about the whole slide.

features.title: Web search configuration
acceptance: Web search SHALL resolve per prompt > role > course > global with the values native, service and off.
Domain allow and block lists and max searches per answer SHALL be enforced.

features.title: Search fallbacks, citations and visible queries
acceptance: Brave, Tavily, Exa and SearXNG fallbacks SHALL work for models without native search (recorded fixtures).
Citations SHALL always render as links showing their host.
Every web query the model makes SHALL be listed in the gloss footer (SEC-24).

features.title: Hedging, circuit breaker, pre-warm
acceptance: WHEN no first token arrives within ai.hedgeAfterMs and a backup is set THEN the request SHALL be duplicated and the loser cancelled.
3 failures in 60 s SHALL open the circuit for 2 minutes.
Connections SHALL be pre-warmed at start and when a lecture opens.

features.title: memory.md from ratings
acceptance: zw with a reason and zg SHALL append learned preferences to memory.md.
The model SHALL never write memory.md on its own (test with an injected instruction).

features.title: Note actions with undo
acceptance: add_flag, add_doubt, add_later, add_office_hours and add_revise SHALL create visible items shown in the gloss.
Each SHALL be undoable with one key.

features.title: Safe rendering of AI output
acceptance: Glosses and notes SHALL render no raw HTML, KaTeX SHALL use trust false and Mermaid strict mode (SEC-22).
A remote image URL in an answer SHALL render as a link chip and no request SHALL leave the webview, asserted in a WebDriver flow (SEC-23).
Links SHALL show their host and open only http(s) after confirmation (SEC-24).

features.title: Provider drift handling
acceptance: Unknown SSE event types and unknown JSON fields SHALL be ignored and counted (ROB-61), tested with the fake provider.
A retired-model error SHALL fall back to the role's next choice or default-fast and tell the user once (ROB-62).

features.title: Spike: vision and TTFT with ChatGPT sign-in
acceptance: With the ChatGPT sign-in stored in the keychain, the F-002 and F-004 measurements SHALL be re-run for OpenAI fast models through scripts/live.sh and appended to their D-entries with a recommendation.
IF the sandbox blocks keychain access THEN the builder SHALL report BLOCKED with the exact command for Jay to run in his own terminal.
features.ask_jay_first: Sign in with ChatGPT in scripts/dev.sh (Settings → Providers) so the spike can use the keychain token?

features.title: Index and passages
acceptance: Sources, slides and notes SHALL be indexed into Tantivy as passages with breadcrumbs, kind, source and lecture fields.
Indexing SHALL be incremental and run at background priority, pausing when the user starts an AI request.
features.try: Add a textbook PDF to sources/: indexing progress shows and finishes

features.title: Section trees and tagging
acceptance: Textbooks and papers SHALL get a section tree from the outline or headings, and passages SHALL not cross sections.
Theorems, definitions, examples and exercises SHALL be tagged by number for exact lookup.

features.title: toc and read tools
acceptance: toc and read tools SHALL navigate the section tree.
read SHALL cap output at 1,500 tokens with a continuation.
read SHALL refuse paths outside the course root.

features.title: Embeddings and tier-1 pre-retrieval
acceptance: index.embeddings SHALL support local-small, local-quality, provider and off, with vectors stored as int8 in vectors.bin and scanned flat.
BM25 and vector results SHALL fuse with RRF (k = 60).
The tier1_p95_ms budget SHALL hold on the fixture course.
features.ask_jay_first: Local embeddings need a model download and possibly ONNX Runtime (native). Approve the runtime and model chosen in the F-003 D-entry?
features.try: Ask about a slide line: the answer cites a textbook passage

features.title: Course card from the syllabus
acceptance: A syllabus in sources/ SHALL trigger one model call producing the course card.
The user SHALL confirm the card before it is saved.
features.try: Drop a syllabus into sources/: Lecter proposes a course card

features.title: Course digest
acceptance: On save, a changed lecture SHALL get a digest of at most 150 tokens from the fast model.
Digests SHALL be produced at most once per 10 minutes per lecture and count against the background cap.
features.try: Open the course digest after two lectures: it lists the main topics

features.title: Past papers
acceptance: Files in pastPapers SHALL split into questions with year, number and marks.
Questions SHALL be tagged with course-card topics, and past_questions SHALL return them.
features.try: Add a past paper: its questions appear under matching topics

features.title: Vision via provider
acceptance: Regions marked for vision SHALL be read by the fast vision model (parsing.vision = provider), returning Markdown, LaTeX and a confidence.
Vision SHALL never run on a page whose text layer passes the confidence check.
features.try: Open a scanned slide: the text appears with a confidence mark

features.title: Render-back confidence
acceptance: Math and tables SHALL be rendered back and compared with the crop.
Confidence SHALL be min(model, match), driving the border tier.

features.title: Local document model option
acceptance: parsing.vision = local SHALL run the local document model in the model worker, loaded on demand and exiting after 60 s idle.
The model download SHALL need consent, show its size, be resumable and be verified by a pinned SHA-256 (SEC-51).
parsing.vision = auto SHALL fall back to the provider below 0.85 confidence.
features.ask_jay_first: The local document model is a native runtime plus a large download. Approve the runtime and model from the F-002 D-entry?

features.title: Figure cards
acceptance: Each figure SHALL get one cached card (what, labels, data, takeaway, confidence).
The card SHALL show as a dotted block and be indexed.
features.try: Open a slide with a chart: a figure card describes it

features.title: search_course and lectures tools
acceptance: search_course SHALL return passages with filters by kind, source and lecture.
lectures SHALL list lectures with digests.

features.title: :find with citations and gd
acceptance: :find SHALL list hits with page citations across the course.
gd SHALL jump to the best source passage for the current block.
features.try: Press gd on a slide line to jump to the textbook passage

features.title: Concept map
acceptance: Definitions and theorems SHALL be linked to lecture blocks and book sections by similarity.
Links SHALL be stored in state.db concepts with no extra model calls.
features.try: Open the concept map: topics from your lectures are linked

features.title: Described figures
acceptance: Vega-Lite, fnplot with sliders, Mermaid (strict), SVG and KaTeX figures SHALL render inside glosses.
Figures SHALL re-render when they scroll into view and SHALL make no network request.
features.try: Ask for a diagram and a plot with a slider

features.title: Page figures in a sandboxed frame
acceptance: Pages SHALL render in an iframe with sandbox allow-scripts only and the CSP of 08-figures.md#sandbox-pages.
Libraries SHALL load only from lecter-lib://, version-pinned.
A WebDriver flow SHALL prove a page cannot fetch, read the parent or call IPC on the CI OSes.
features.try: Ask for an explorable diagram: it runs in its own frame and stops when hidden

features.title: Figure watchdog and live-frame limit
acceptance: A frame busy over 2 s or over 150 MB SHALL be replaced by its static image.
At most figures.maxLiveFrames frames SHALL be live; off-screen frames SHALL be replaced by their static image and restored.

features.title: Figure proposals: Ask
acceptance: propose_figure SHALL produce a card with kind, tier, token and time estimates.
y, 2, n and A, and their keycap buttons, SHALL act on the card.
features.try: Open a slide with a graph: Lecter offers a figure with a time and cost estimate

features.title: Figure proposals: Auto and precedence
acceptance: Mode SHALL resolve per prompt > role > course > global, with defaults auto for described and ask for pages.
Auto SHALL build the cheaper option and then show the upgrade card.
Figure generation SHALL never delay the text answer's first token (timed test).

features.title: Figure storage and static export
acceptance: Each figure SHALL save its source and a static render under lectures/assets/<lecture>/.
The gloss SHALL reference both, and Markdown viewers SHALL see the static image.

features.title: Dashboard panels
acceptance: The dashboard SHALL show every panel in 11-dashboard.md#panels with live data from lectures and course.md.
The dashboard SHALL be lazy-loaded (not in the main chunk).
features.try: Open the dashboard: flags, doubts and lectures are listed

features.title: course.md sync
acceptance: Edits in course.md SHALL appear on the dashboard within 1 s.
Edits on the dashboard SHALL be written to course.md within 1 s.

features.title: Dashboard row actions
acceptance: Each row action SHALL work by key.
Each row action SHALL work by its hover button and context menu.
features.try: Resolve a doubt from the dashboard: it disappears from the list

features.title: Revise sessions
acceptance: A revise session SHALL ask one question at a time.
A miss SHALL be explained in at most 120 words.
Related items SHALL be resolved only after the user confirms.
The session SHALL save a summary to course.md.
features.try: Start a revise session from the dashboard

features.title: Ask the course
acceptance: The dashboard chat SHALL answer course-wide questions using tiers 0–2.
An answer SHALL be saveable to course.md → Notes on S.
features.try: Ask the whole course a question from the dashboard

features.title: Onboarding steps
acceptance: First run SHALL show the 8 onboarding steps, each skippable.
Choices SHALL write settings.
:tutor SHALL reopen onboarding.
features.try: Start with LECTER_TEST_HOME set to an empty folder: onboarding runs

features.title: Tutorial course content
acceptance: A bundled "Lecter 101" course SHALL contain one plain-English lecture about using Lecter, generated from Markdown at build time.
Its answers SHALL be canned placeholders labelled "Sample answer", needing no provider, key or network.
The tutorial and its assets SHALL contain no content from tests/corpus/private (scripts/check_private.py passes on them).
features.try: Open Lecter 101 offline: sample glosses show without a provider

features.title: Tutorial checklist
acceptance: The checklist SHALL tick itself as each task is done: open slides, a, s, D, mm, ask about a figure, zg, open the dashboard.
Each task SHALL show the click way and the key way.
features.try: Do the Lecter 101 tutorial end to end

features.title: Feedback sharing opt-in
acceptance: Sharing SHALL be off unless opted in, and text SHALL need a second opt-in.
A sample payload SHALL be shown.
Data SHALL stay local until feedback.endpoint is set.

features.title: Export to Markdown
acceptance: :export md SHALL write a clean Markdown file with static figure images.
The export SHALL never overwrite an existing file without asking.
features.try: Export a lecture to Markdown and open it in another editor

features.title: Export to PDF and LaTeX via Pandoc
acceptance: :export pdf and :export tex SHALL run the installed Pandoc with a fixed argument list (no shell, no user-controlled flags).
WHEN Pandoc is missing THEN the command SHALL explain how to install it.
features.try: Export a lecture to PDF (needs Pandoc installed)

features.title: Model worker sandbox
acceptance: The model worker SHALL run under the same OS sandboxes as the parse worker, with no network.
The escape tests SHALL pass on all three CI OSes.

features.title: Tauri lockdown audit
acceptance: Each window SHALL have its own capability file listing only commands it calls (a test diffs capabilities against the bindings usage).
A test SHALL load the release config and assert the CSP of SEC-30 and devtools off.
Dropped paths SHALL be canonicalised and checked (SEC-35), tested with symlink and traversal fixtures.

features.title: Nightly fuzzing and regression flow
acceptance: nightly.yml SHALL run every fuzz target for 10 minutes and upload crash inputs.
A seeded crash input SHALL become a regression test in tests/fixtures/fuzz-regressions/ (documented flow, proven once).

features.title: Licence notices and pinned downloads
acceptance: About → Licences SHALL list every Rust crate and npm package with its licence text, generated at build time (SEC-52).
Every downloaded binary or model SHALL be verified against a pinned SHA-256 before use (SEC-51), with a test feeding a tampered file.

features.title: Release workflow and draft release
acceptance: WHEN a tag v*.*.* is pushed THEN release.yml SHALL build every package in 01-architecture.md#packaging.
The packages, SBOMs, SHA256SUMS and latest.json SHALL be attached to a draft GitHub release whose body comes from CHANGELOG.md.
Release artifacts SHALL contain no files from tests/ and no debug-only hooks (release-check).

features.title: Signing where credentials exist
acceptance: WHERE signing secrets are present the packages SHALL be signed and macOS builds notarised.
WHERE they are absent the workflow SHALL succeed and the release notes SHALL say the build is unsigned.
verify: release.yml dry run with and without secrets

features.title: Signed in-app updates
acceptance: WHEN an installed build sees a newer signed latest.json THEN the app SHALL offer the update.
The updater SHALL verify the signature before installing and reject a tampered manifest (test).
features.try: Check for updates in About: it says you are up to date

features.title: Installer identity
acceptance: The Windows installer SHALL use a fixed WiX upgradeCode recorded in a D-entry.
The NSIS install folder SHALL use the product name, not the identifier.

features.title: Nightly perf matrix, chaos and soak
acceptance: nightly.yml SHALL run budgets.sh on ubuntu-24.04, macos-15 and windows-2025, including installer_mb from a release-profile bundle.
The chaos job SHALL prove hedging, circuit breaking, retry-after handling and Esc-cancel against every fake-provider scenario.
The soak job SHALL run 30 minutes nightly and 3 hours on Sundays, failing if memory grows over 10% or keystroke p99 leaves its budget.

features.title: Accessibility: names and keyboard
acceptance: All controls SHALL have accessible names.
Every control SHALL be reachable by keyboard with a visible focus ring.
features.try: Use the app for two minutes without the mouse

features.title: Accessibility: axe, motion and contrast
acceptance: axe checks in e2e SHALL report no serious or critical violations on every main screen.
Reduced motion SHALL make keycap presses and overlay fades instant.
Amber confidence borders SHALL also carry a text badge.

features.title: Visual baselines per OS
acceptance: tests/visual SHALL compare WebDriver screenshots of the main screens with per-OS baselines, failing above a 0.5% pixel difference.
Baseline files SHALL be protected, so only a Jay-approved feature can change them.
features.ask_jay_first: Approve the first set of per-OS screenshot baselines (the orchestrator shows them before merging)?
